summary.text: 球 combines 玉, which marks the jade category, with 求 as its phonetic element. It is associated with jade and jade chimes; its current ball sense is explained as reuse of the graph for the word associated with 毬, though that word’s early pronunciation is not independently established.

formation.text: 球 is a phonosemantic compound: 玉 contributes the jade category, while 求 supplies a sound cue. The modern Mandarin readings of both are qiú; in Baxter–Sagart’s reconstruction they share Middle Chinese gjuw, while their Old Chinese forms differ slightly. These comparisons fit the traditional analysis but do not independently prove the ancient sound relation. The curated seal-style drawing is a modern rendering, not an ancient witness.

components.text: 玉 is the left-hand component and contributes the jade category. Early forms of 玉 are described as jade pieces strung together, but this does not establish 球’s own ancient graphic development.
求 is the right-hand phonetic element. A separate account suggests a winding or rolling association, but does not establish that 求 contributes this meaning in 球.

sound_limitation.text: The historical dictionary identifies 求 as phonetic. Modern and reconstructed readings provide comparisons, but do not independently establish the precise ancient sound relation.

sound.text: 求 and 球 share the modern Mandarin reading qiú and the Middle Chinese form gjuw in Baxter–Sagart’s system. Their Old Chinese reconstructions are 求 *[g](r)u and 球 *[g](r)[u], a similar but not identical comparison compatible with the traditional phonetic analysis.

history.text: The curated seal-style drawing shows the traditional analysis of 玉 on the left and 求 on the right. It illustrates that account but does not document an ancient form or a sequence of graphic changes.

A secondary account places 球 in Qin-period writing, though the precise early form is not confirmed by a primary witness here. In 戛擊鳴球, 球 is interpreted as referring to jade chimes; the quotation does not date the surviving wording or graph.

Historical accounts distinguish 球’s jade association from 毬’s use for a ball and propose that 球 was reused to write the ball word. This is a proposed sound-based borrowing, not a demonstrated change from ‘jade’ to ‘ball’; the early ball word’s name or pronunciation is not independently established.
A reported Tang-era statement links 毬’s spelling to a pronunciation change in 鞠. It does not establish 毬’s exact first occurrence or complete graphic history.

uncertainties.text: The Qin-period dating is reported secondarily, and the precise early graph has not been confirmed by a primary witness. The jade-chime passage does not date the surviving wording or character.

The proposed borrowing of 球 for the ball word associated with 毬 lacks an independently supported early name or sound comparison for that word; the earliest dated use of 球 for ‘ball’ remains unresolved.
求’s phonetic role is stated in the historical dictionary analysis. The available reading and reconstruction comparisons do not independently establish the exact ancient sound relation.

senses.text: Historical dictionary accounts gloss 球 as jade. The reported Qin-period writing does not securely establish the earliest attested sense.
In 戛擊鳴球, 球 is interpreted as a jade chime. The passage does not securely date the surviving wording or graph.

球 means a ball or spherical object. Its use for the ball word associated with 毬 is explained as borrowing, not as an established semantic extension from jade; the earliest dated use remains unresolved.

senses.period: late nineteenth century in cited Japanese examples
senses.text: Japanese examples from 1872 and 1873 use 球 for a geometric sphere, including the sun. They document usage at those dates, not the sense’s earliest appearance.

developments.text: The jade-chime use is documented, but the evidence does not show whether it developed from a broader jade sense or named an object independently.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a continuous semantic path from jade or jade chimes to ‘ball’; the ball sense is instead explained as borrowing 球 for the word associated with 毬.
Dictionary glosses and the literary example do not establish a hypothetical original meaning or a securely dated earliest attestation.

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, quoted in the character-specific entry by 中央纪委国家监委网站
evidence.text: The article reports that 球 is first seen in Qin-period writing, formed from 玉 as meaning element and 求 as phonetic element; it quotes the Shuowen gloss as “jade.” It describes 球 used for a round ball as a later borrowing of 毬. This is a modern secondary account of the historical dictionary and graphic record, not an inspected Qin manuscript witness.
evidence.title: 〖每日一字〗球：美玉？

evidence.source: 《尚書·益稷》 passage as reproduced by 文林社
evidence.text: The passage reads “戛擊鳴球” and its accompanying explanation identifies 鳴球 as struck jade chimes. This gives an early literary use associated with a jade sound-producing object; the page describes the work as a pre-Qin compilation, but the wording alone does not date the graph or establish the manuscript age of this passage.
evidence.kind: primary text in a modern transcription
evidence.title: 虞書·夔曰：“戛擊鳴球……”

evidence.source: コトバンク, 精選版 日本国語大辞典
evidence.text: The entry gives 1872 医語類聚 as an example for the technical geometric sense of 球, then cites an 1873 school reader sentence defining the sun as a large 球. These examples document late nineteenth-century Japanese usage, not the earliest Chinese use of the graph or word.

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 entry quoted in 中央纪委国家监委网站
evidence.text: The article quotes the Shuowen definition 鞠丸也 and analysis 从毛求聲: 毛 is the semantic element and 求 the phonetic element. It says this entry is in the later-added section (說文新附) and explains 毬 as a ball-like game object. The dictionary statement is historical evidence of an account, not by itself proof of the character's first attestation.

evidence.field: historical distinction between 鞠 and 毬
evidence.text: The article quotes the Tang-era statement “近俗聲訛謂鞠為毬，字亦從而變焉，非古也,” presenting 毬 as a later graphic form associated with a changed pronunciation of 鞠. The source thus disputes treating 毬 as the oldest form of the ball word. It does not supply a manuscript witness or precise first date for 毬.
evidence.title: 〖每日一字〗球：美玉？

evidence.source: 中央纪委国家监委网站
evidence.text: The account separates the old jade sense of 球 from use for round objects, which it treats as a borrowing from 毬. It describes 毛-filled balls and later usage of 毬 for round objects more generally. It cites Tang records of 打毬 and later Song usage, but those examples establish historical use of 毬 rather than the precise date when 球 began replacing it.
evidence.title: 〖每日一字〗球：美玉？

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No 球-specific oracle bone, bronze, or Qin manuscript facsimile/inscription was opened; the reported Qin-period first attestation is from a secondary article, so its exact form and dating remain unchecked.

The pre-Qin literary context of 鳴球 as a jade chime is supported by the quoted text and later traditional commentary, but the date of the surviving textual wording and its graph cannot be inferred from the work's traditional setting.

Sources conflict in emphasis: Shuowen-derived explanations say 玉 is semantic and 求 phonetic; the consulted Japanese dictionary adds a possible rolling/winding semantic association for 求. Independent evidence for 求 contributing that meaning to 球 was not found.
The relation between 鞠 and 毬 as spellings of the ball word is reported by a secondary source quoting 封氏聞見記; no independent manuscript history or exact first date for 毬 was established.

The semantic transition from a jade chime/name to a generic spherical object is not demonstrated as a continuous metaphorical chain. The sourced account instead proposes lexical borrowing of 球 for 毬; exact earliest dated 球-as-ball attestation remains unresolved.

No independently supported historical reconstruction for 求 was available in the supplied exact local rows, so no Baxter–Sagart within-system sound comparison between 求 and 球 is asserted. Modern qiú readings are not ancient phonological proof.
Official Unicode character-specific Unihan endpoints for U+7403 and U+6BEC could not be opened. Local rows were checked, but the requested official click-through record was not verified.
No glyph images were inspected. The source references do not establish possible graphic corruption or variant development for 球's ancient forms.

No evidence here establishes the actual early name or pronunciation of a physical ball object as a basis for a sound-based whole-graph loan; the proposed borrowing is a graphic/lexical claim reported by the secondary account, and the independent source-word pronunciation evidence remains insufficient.
No 球-specific Qin manuscript or inscription was opened; the claim of Qin-period first attestation comes from the inspected secondary account, and the precise ancient graph cannot be checked here.

The Shuowen-derived role assignment 玉 semantic + 求 phonetic is directly reported in the official dictionary entry. No independently checked ancient phonological comparison for 求 was available, so the phonetic role is reported as the dictionary analysis, not independently demonstrated by reconstructions.

Sources distinguish 球’s jade and ball senses by proposing a borrowing from 毬; a continuous metaphorical semantic path is not established. The opened sources do not give a securely dated earliest 球-as-ball occurrence.

The early object name/pronunciation of a physical ball is not independently established here; do not claim an independently demonstrated sound-based borrowing from the object’s name. The secondary account describes a graph/word substitution 球借作毬.
The reported earliest 球 appearance in Qin writing and variant 璆 were not checked against a primary paleographic witness, leaving possible graphic variation or corruption unresolved.

The Shangshu “戛擊鳴球” quotation page was inaccessible during this run; the Taiwan dictionary independently records the passage and interprets 球 as a jade chime, but that does not date the surviving text or graph.
Direct Unicode Unihan character records for 球 and 毬 could not be verified; local reading rows were cross-checked as supplied data only.
No exact Commons description page for a 毬 historical glyph or character-specific Xiaoxuetang form was established; only the better-sourced 球 seal-style redraw is proposed.
The local Baxter–Sagart data supplied a 球 row but no 求 row, so same-system historical sound comparison remains a gap.

The supplied exact local Baxter–Sagart rows show 求 *[g](r)u and 球 *[g](r)[u], with shared MC gjuw; the external Baxter–Sagart source could not be opened in this pass, so these local rows should not be represented as newly verified external evidence.

Official character-specific Unihan records for 求 and 球 could not be opened. Local kMandarin rows report qiú for both, but remain local data in this pass; modern readings are not evidence of ancient sound correspondence.

The inspected account proposes that 球 was borrowed for the ball word written 毬, but no independently verified early name or pronunciation for the physical ball or word was obtained. Keep the proposed graphic/lexical borrowing distinct from a proven sound-based loan.
No primary paleographic witness or independently dated earliest attestation for 球 as ‘ball’ was inspected. The history and chronology of the jade and ball senses therefore remain partly unresolved.

The review-requested learner explanation should say the secondary account proposes reusing 球 for the ball word associated with 毬, while noting that the early word/object name and pronunciation are not independently established. The current evidence supports a proposed lexical/graphic substitution, not a proven sound-based borrowing mechanism.
No primary Qin manuscript or paleographic witness for 球 was opened; its reported Qin-period first appearance remains secondary. No physical graphic lineage or corruption history is established.
The earliest dated use of 球 for ‘ball’ remains unresolved. The sources separate the jade sense from ball-word use, but do not securely date when 球 began replacing 毬.
The link from 球’s jade sense to its jade-chime use is not established as a specific semantic development; surviving textual wording and graph dating remain uncertain.

The exact Xiaoxuetang 毬 query record was unavailable (cache miss), so its specific candidate image was not selected. The proposed Commons 毬 seal-style vector is a modern redraw; it does not show an ancient artifact or graphic lineage.
